item.title: Are Houthis now facing a nuclear power? Pakistan declares it will defend MBS 'to any extent'
item.description: Pakistan has delivered its strongest defence pledge to Saudi Arabia as escalating Houthi attacks put Riyadh’s alliances to the test. Military spokesperson Lt. Gen. Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Islamabad stands with the Kingdom both “diplomatically and physically” and would go “to any extent” required by Saudi leadership. But Pakistan has not committed to direct military action against the Houthis, while the new Saudi-Pakistan-Türkiye collective-defence pact remains untested in combat. With Riyadh under growing pressure, will MBS’ allies actually enter the fight or keep pushing diplomacy?

item.title: Russia attack confirmed, Kaliningrad next? Poland locks down airspace, Moldova hit by ghost flights
item.description: Eastern Europe is on edge as Russia’s expanding drone war triggers fresh security alarms beyond Ukraine. Poland scrambled military aircraft and placed air-defence and radar systems on heightened readiness during a Russian jet-powered drone attack, although Warsaw later reported no breach of Polish airspace. Meanwhile, Moldova reported several unidentified aircraft crossing its territory, with fragments and an explosion site later found inside Ukraine just 1.2 km from the border. The scares came amid another large Russian aerial barrage. How close is the drone war getting to Europe’s borders?

item.title: Putin’s 'accidental' strike plan revealed? Europe warns Russia may test NATO with drones & missiles
item.description: European leaders are raising alarms over what they describe as an intensifying Russian hybrid threat, amid fears of drone incursions, missile incidents, sabotage, cyberattacks and pressure on critical infrastructure. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Moscow could allegedly target NATO’s eastern flank with drones or missiles and portray any strike as an “accident” to undermine an alliance response. French President Emmanuel Macron said Russia’s hybrid threat to Europe and France had intensified, ordering plans to secure critical infrastructure and sensitive defence-industrial sites against drone and cyber threats. European governments are now reviewing preparedness as tensions over Russia’s war in Ukraine deepen.
